items.text: The German government considered the latest US plan for Gaza an opportunity to advance the disarmament of Hamas. The German Foreign Ministry spokesperson noted the complexity of the plan and the presence of disagreements and unanswered questions. More details were provided in an interview with Ali Hassanpour.

Mohammad Taghi Neghdali, a member of the Judiciary Commission of the Parliament, called for the notification and implementation of the Hijab law by the Supreme National Security Council. He described women's optional dress as a "naked coup" and part of a "war." These statements aim to legitimize government intervention in women's dress and lifestyle and increase pressure for mandatory hijab enforcement.

Ali Motahari expressed certainty that Masoud Pezeshkian will not resign. Mohammad Baqer Kharazi stated that Pezeshkian has attempted to resign 28 times. Kharazi was summoned to the Special Clergy Court following these statements.

Mojtaba Khamenei appointed his military advisor to the highest security body of the Islamic Republic. Mohsen Rezaei warned about internal unrest. He is described as Mojtaba's arm for external and internal conflict with the people.

General Ahmad Vahidi was appointed as the commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps with the rank of Major General. General Ali Abdollahi was named Chief of the Armed Forces General Staff, and Kiomarth Heydari was appointed as his deputy. Hossein Taeb was assigned as the head of the Basij Organization.
Mojtaba Khamenei appointed six commanders in the Armed Forces Headquarters, the IRGC, and Basij. Ahmad Vahidi was appointed as the commander of the IRGC. Mostafa Izadi was appointed as his deputy.

Esteghlal Club reformed its cycling team on the anniversary of the death of Parviz Khosrowani, the club's founder. This move is described as a return to the club's historical identity. The club also highlighted Khosrowani's important role in the formation of Esteghlal.

Soheila Hosseini, a detained citizen of Mashhad, was released from Vakilabad prison after posting a 4 billion toman bail. This release took place on Monday, 19th of Mordad. Harana News Agency reported this news.
A man in Sari was killed by his wife through administering methadone pills. The suspect has been arrested by the police.

Mojtaba Khamenei appointed Hossein Taeb as the head of the Basij organization. Taeb previously led the Intelligence Organization of the IRGC and was a senior advisor to the commander of the IRGC. He is on the US and EU sanctions lists for human rights violations.

Donald Trump stated that representatives of the Islamic Republic of Iran have demanded compensation for damages from the recent five-month military conflict. In response, he demanded compensation from Iran for deaths and injuries caused by Iranian actions. Trump has ordered that this issue be firmly raised in future negotiations.

Javad Nodehi, a political detainee related to the December 1404 protests, has been in legal limbo in Sabzevar prison for over seven months. Despite bail being posted, he has been denied temporary release. He also has no access to his chosen lawyer.

The family of Lindsey and Greg Foreman announced that the two British citizens ended their hunger strike after about three months in Evin prison. The couple was arrested in January 2025 in Iran and sentenced to 10 years in prison. Their child said the parents decided to end the strike to regain their physical strength.

Italy seeks a more active role in the Middle East amid security and political crises. The Italian foreign minister emphasized the importance of Rome-Riyadh relations. Saudi Arabia was described as an essential partner for regional stability.

The Chief of Staff of the Israeli Army stated in a meeting with the CENTCOM commander that the army's historic achievements must be preserved and strengthened. He emphasized that the army is fully prepared for an immediate return to heavy combat. The CENTCOM commander also highlighted the strategic cooperation between the US and Israeli armies.

Donald Trump stated in a recent post that Iran should be held responsible for the damages and deaths in Lebanon, Syria, Yemen, and Gaza. These remarks were made in the context of Iran negotiations. Trump made this statement one hour ago.

The Internal Affairs Commission of the Parliament approved five articles of the strategic action plan for the sustainable security of the Strait of Hormuz and the Persian Gulf. One of the key approved items is the prohibition of transit of equipment owned by the US, Israel, and hostile countries through the Strait of Hormuz. The review of other articles of the plan has been postponed to future sessions.

About 250 workers at Madkoush Steel Company in Bandar Abbas were dismissed by the employer. The company is located in the special economic zone of mineral and metal industries of the Persian Gulf. The layoffs have recently taken place.

Mohsen Rezaei was appointed as the representative of Mojtaba Khamenei in the Supreme National Security Council. He was also assigned as the secretary of the council by Masoud Pezeshkian. The Supreme National Security Council is one of the most important decision-making bodies in security and foreign policy.

The audio version of the Titraval program with Niusha Saremi has been released. The program mentions changes in commanders and the return of Taeb by the order of Mojtaba Khamenei. The topic of security reorganization in Iran is also discussed.

Jaber Rajabi said that Mojtaba Khamenei's recent appointments and increased activities may indicate his more public presence. He added that appointing Hossein Taeb as the commander of Basij shows planning to rely on a core group of supporters. These developments could lead to an increased role of Basij in the power structure.

At least 9 protest gatherings were held today, Monday, 19 Mordad, by retirees of telecommunications and the Steel Retirement Fund of Isfahan in various cities. These protests continued for the third consecutive day. The cities of Bijar, Arak, Ahvaz, Isfahan, Kermanshah, Sanandaj, Ardabil, and Tehran hosted these protests.

Manchester United's negotiations to hire Jose Mourinho as Sir Alex Ferguson's successor lasted for weeks and initially reached an agreement. However, Mourinho withdrew due to a promise to Chelsea and family reasons. Subsequently, Manchester United appointed David Moyes as the new manager.

Hossein Ali Hajideligani criticized the government's economic performance in a parliamentary session, stating the government lacks an economic plan and called for the formation of an economic war room. He linked the rise in prices of essential goods, cars, and exchange rates to government policies. He also expressed concern that the Caspian Sea convention would reduce Iran's share.

Brent crude oil prices in the market surpassed $84. The reason for this increase is cited as the uncertain situation in the Strait of Hormuz. American officials told Axios that eight million barrels of oil are exported daily from the Strait of Hormuz in coordination with the US military.

Shayan Mohammadi remains in an uncertain detention status in Sheiban Prison in Ahvaz after 22 days of arrest. His case is still unresolved, and he is denied contact and visitation with his family. This information was confirmed by a source close to his family.

Mehdi Taj announced that the new season of Iranian football league will be held with spectators. After the National Iranian Revolution in December 1404, matches were mostly held without spectators. No matches in Tehran had spectators.

Benjamin Netanyahu rejected the 15-point peace plan led by the US and stated that the Israeli army will not withdraw from Gaza until Hamas is truly disarmed. He also said that as long as he is prime minister, no independent Palestinian state will be established in Gaza or the West Bank. Meir Javdanfar explained Israel's opposition to a Palestinian state is due to the experience of withdrawing from Gaza and its transformation into a base for armed groups.

The Iranian Foreign Ministry stated that reopening the Strait of Hormuz depends on the lifting of the US naval blockade. The parliament approved the general framework of a plan to ensure the sustainable security of the Strait of Hormuz and the Persian Gulf. This plan aims to turn the Islamic Republic's policies regarding the strait into law.

Donald Trump emphasized US Navy control over the Strait of Hormuz, stating they have established an unbreakable blockade like a steel wall, denying ship entry to Iran while keeping the route open for others. He also announced mine-clearing in the strait and described Iran as bankrupt with no money.

The International Atomic Energy Agency will soon remove the remaining nuclear materials from Syria's Site 99 following secret agreements between the Trump administration, Israel, and Syria. These materials are insufficient for nuclear weapons but raised concerns about use in a dirty bomb. An agreement between Damascus and the agency for safe transfer of these materials was signed three weeks ago.

Morad Vaisi said Mojtaba Khamenei considers the future uprising of the people as the most significant threat to the Islamic Republic. Basij is at the forefront of suppressing protests. Hossein Taeb has been appointed as a trusted person at the head of Basij.

Donald Trump stated that the Islamic Republic has demanded compensation in negotiations. He said the United States can also claim compensation for damages caused by the Islamic Republic. Trump referred to incidents such as the USS Cole and the protesters killed in recent months.

Verbal tensions between Iranian and US officials have increased amid more complex negotiations. Donald Trump responded to Iran's compensation request by stating that Iran should pay for damages over the past 50 years and the killing of protesters. This report was published by Niloufar Mansouri from Iran International.

Masoud Pezeshkian had a seven-hour meeting with Mojtaba Khamenei discussing various issues including people's livelihood, market, employment, housing, and sanctions. He emphasized that Mojtaba Khamenei was in full health. The outcome of this conversation was one word: "unity."

Mojtaba Khamenei announced his power arrangement by issuing six military and two non-military orders. Ahmad Vahidi was appointed head of the IRGC, Hossein Taeb as head of the Basij, and Mohsen Rezaei to the Supreme National Security Council. These orders signal the continuation of internal repression and external adventurism.

Johan Wadephul, Germany's foreign minister, has called on the Islamic Republic to engage constructively in talks with regional neighbors and the US. He emphasized that the Strait of Hormuz must be reopened unconditionally. The aim is to end conflicts and ensure free and safe navigation.

Reuters reported that the Nasdaq and S&P 500 indices fell, and shares of chipmakers like Intel and Nvidia declined. The drop occurred as investors grew less confident about reaching an agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

Brent oil prices rose close to $87 per barrel. Iran has linked the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz to conditions including the end of the US blockade. Attacks by Houthis and disruptions in ship traffic have increased concerns in energy markets.

Verbal tensions between US and Iranian officials have increased. The Trump administration has maintained sanctions and the blockade of Iranian ports. These sanctions have exerted more pressure on the Islamic Republic than military attacks.

The Yemeni army announced that the Houthi militias targeted residential neighborhoods in Marib with ballistic missiles and drones. Al Hadath network reported that the Houthis also shelled the port city of Mocha. These attacks were carried out by Tehran's proxy group.

The International Atomic Energy Agency will soon remove nuclear materials stored at a secret site in Syria with the approval of the Damascus government. This action follows months of negotiations between the US, Israel, Syria, and the agency. The transfer is expected to be completed before the end of the year.

Donald Trump published a chart showing the decline in the value of the Iranian rial during his second term as president. The value of one million rials dropped from one dollar and eleven cents to fifty-three cents. Trump described this decrease as the rial's value going "into the trash."

The Washington Post reported that a threat from the Islamic Republic to kill Donald Trump led to a special operation in which Trump secretly flew from Turkey on a military plane. The White House announced Trump was on Air Force One, but he was secretly transferred to a smaller plane using a food truck. This method of using Air Force One as a decoy plane has been used before in serious threat situations.

Ehsan Khandozi warned about street unrest and the possibility of a third war. He stated that the experience of the 12-day war and the December unrest shows the danger of wrong decisions. Khandozi emphasized that there is a 100 to 120-day window to make major shifts with new partners.

The Washington Post reported that a threat from Iran to assassinate Trump led to a secret operation in which Trump left Turkey on a replacement military plane. The White House claimed he was on Air Force One, but he was secretly transferred to a smaller plane. This operation was carried out without the knowledge of reporters and some White House staff.

Republican Senator Tom Cotton told Fox News that the people of Iran are the first and worst victims of the revolutionary extremists who rule Iran today and deserve a much better future. He added that America should always stand with the forces and friends of freedom. Cotton said that help is on the way and the people of Iran must regain their freedom and destiny.

Hamid Hosseini, spokesperson for the Iranian Petroleum, Gas, and Petrochemical Exporters Union, stated that Masoud Pezeshkian's government is pursuing an energy card plan for each family. This card includes quotas for gasoline, gas, and electricity. Families can sell their surplus quota on the energy exchange.

The head of the Iran-China Chamber of Commerce warned about the severe consequences of the maritime blockade of Iran's southern ports by the US. He stated that this situation could impose significant additional costs on Iran's economy and worsen economic problems. He also emphasized that the blockade should end through negotiation or other means.

Kayhan newspaper referred to the defense pact of Mecca between Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan as a betrayal by puppet rulers in Islamic lands. It spoke of the awakening of young Muslims and the resistance of groups like Hezbollah Lebanon and the resistance in Iraq and Yemen. Kayhan emphasized that the dignity of Muslims lies in resistance and the governance of the Guardianship of the Islamic Jurist.

Shayan Samiei commented on Donald Trump's statements about control of the Strait of Hormuz. He said Trump wants to convey that the Islamic Republic is no longer militarily capable of setting the rules in the Strait of Hormuz.

Mohammad Ghaedi, an international relations expert, said that the Islamic Republic may be seeking to prolong negotiations until the US elections and strengthen its bargaining leverage by raising the issue of compensation again in the Tehran-Washington talks.

Kamyar Behrang stated that after the killing of IRGC leaders by Israel and the US, some positions have become vacant and need to be filled. He said the new appointments in the Islamic Republic's structure are linked to recent changes in the Supreme National Security Council. Mojtaba Khamenei aims to consolidate influence and form a network of loyal forces, with a focus on strengthening intelligence and internal repression structures.

The Washington Post, citing reviewed documents, reported that the Islamic Republic's threat to kill Donald Trump last month caused the US President to leave Turkey in a secret and rare operation on a military plane. The newspaper wrote that despite the White House announcement that Trump flew on Air Force One, after boarding in front of cameras, he was secretly transferred in an airport food truck to a smaller US Air Force plane.

Iran's missile and drone threats have led Gulf Arab countries to expand their security cooperation with the United States. Tehran's efforts to gain more control over the Strait of Hormuz could complicate Iran-China relations. This report was published by Alireza Mohibi from Iran International.

Esmaeil Baghai, spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, stated that the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz is conditional on the lifting of the US naval blockade. In talks with Oman, there was no discussion about charging tolls on ships. The Islamic Republic seeks to receive fees for maritime services.

Donald Trump outlined the options the US has against the Islamic Republic, including continuing current pressures, military attack, and economic pressure. He described Iran's economic situation as critical, with inflation at 300% and soldiers' salaries unpaid. Trump emphasized that the US can either maintain this situation or deliver a military strike.

Citizens say inflation and rising costs have made going to cafes and leisure activities impossible for many. Medical and rent expenses have become priorities, and leisure activities have been eliminated. Some people are even struggling to meet their basic needs.

Houshang Hassaniyari referred to Donald Trump's statements about demanding compensation from the Islamic Republic and said that the reciprocal compensation claims from Tehran and Washington will complicate negotiations. He believes this issue will make reaching a compromise more difficult.

Donald Trump stated that removing Gianni Infantino from FIFA presidency would be a disastrous mistake. He defended Infantino's role in organizing the most successful World Cup. These remarks came after criticisms from UEFA, CONCACAF, and AFC.
A group of retired telecommunications workers gathered in Isfahan on Monday, 19 Mordad. They chanted slogans against the IRGC. These videos were received by Iran International.

Houthi forces attacked a commercial cargo ship in the Bab al-Mandab Strait early Tuesday, August 11, resulting in the death of three crew members. The attack was carried out with a ballistic missile, and the victims included two Pakistani and one Indonesian nationals. Additionally, the Houthis launched dozens of drones and missiles towards the port and city of Al-Mokha.

Hossein Hosseinzadeh, chairman of the Persian Gulf Holding, announced talks with several economic entities and wealthy supporters for the sale of Esteghlal Club. This process requires approval from relevant authorities and could lead to economic and managerial stability for the club if successful. Previously, governmental bodies showed no real intention for genuine privatization of Esteghlal.

A large fire broke out at the Zawiya oil refinery in Libya. The National Oil Corporation of Libya announced that a drone crash near the tanks was the third attack in two days. The refinery's operations have been completely halted.

Nurses at Hakim Hospital in Nishapur protested against unpaid dues, bonuses, lack of equipment and staff, forced overtime, and mismanagement. They chanted the slogan "Bonuses are our right, the money is in your pocket." The protest took place on Tuesday, August 11.
Avat Karami, an environmental activist from Sanandaj, was arrested by security forces at his home. The arrest took place on the evening of Sunday, August 9. His place of detention is unknown.

The Bel cafe restaurant in the Valenjak area of Tehran was sealed by relevant authorities. The reason for this action has not yet been announced by officials. It is likely that this sealing is part of recent crackdowns on businesses and public places.

A senior Israeli official described the Mecca defense agreement between Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan as concerning and against Israel. He mentioned the possibility of Egypt joining this coalition and suggested forming alternative alliances centered on Greece, Cyprus, India, and the UAE. He also emphasized Israel's need for a comprehensive plan to strengthen its military capabilities.

Three Sunni brothers named Jihad, Baqer, and Foad Shavardi were arrested on Sunday, 18 Mordad, by the Intelligence Corps agents in Shadegan. The arrest took place at their private homes in the city of Fallahiyeh, Shadegan. They were transferred to an unknown location after the arrest.

The deputy prosecutor of Ardabil announced the closure of three cafes and the arrest of 16 people for violating Islamic values and norms. The violations included gambling, breaking social norms, and promoting corruption. Additionally, the cafe restaurant "Bol" in Tehran was also closed.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations reported an incident in the Sea of Oman involving a tanker and military forces. No further details about the incident have been released. Investigations are ongoing, and ships have been advised to remain vigilant.

Lionel Messi has indefinitely suspended his football activities following the death of his father, Jorge Messi. Jorge passed away at the age of 68 and played a significant role in Lionel's life and career. Messi has not set a date to return to Inter Miami yet.

Ruhollah Rahimpor, a journalist and political analyst, said the Trump administration is simultaneously pursuing three strategies: maintaining the military option, intensifying economic and political pressure, and increasing pressure on the internal structure of the Islamic Republic. He added that as long as the naval blockade, sanctions, and US military presence in the region continue, there is no sign of any of these strategies being abandoned.

Mojtaba Khamenei has appointed new military commanders. These appointments aim to manage wartime conditions and strengthen readiness for a possible confrontation with the US and Israel. Additionally, an order was issued to merge the General Staff of the Armed Forces and Khatam al-Anbiya Headquarters to enhance coordination between the IRGC and the army.

The Criminal Court of Damascus sentenced Bashar al-Assad and several other former Syrian officials to death. Charges include intentional murder, torture leading to death, arbitrary detention, and crimes against humanity. Bashar al-Assad was tried in absentia and found guilty.

Milad Balsini, a Turk (Azerbaijani) activist, was summoned to the Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor's Office in Tabriz. A notice from Branch 15 of the prosecutor's office was issued to him. He must appear within five days to defend against the alleged accusation.

Warning SMS messages about ration cards have been sent to household heads by the Ministry of Welfare system. The messages state that continuation of ration card payments is conditional on in-person visits and identity verification. Payments will be stopped if individuals do not visit in person.

Workers and citizens in various Iranian cities have reported economic difficulties and reduced public services. Prices of goods and services have increased, and issues such as power outages and weak internet are present. There are also concerns about rising theft and pressure on nurses.

The German Foreign Ministry announced that the consular and visa section of its embassy in Tehran is still operating in emergency mode and no regular appointments for visa applications are scheduled. Previously submitted visa applications are being processed, and a separate process is in place for family reunification applicants. Registration for students and doctors has been possible since July 15, but appointment times have not yet been announced.

The Association for the Support of Children's Rights reported that sexual abuse of children was one of the most frequent legal cases in 1404. Economic problems, fear of social stigma, and lack of specialized lawyers were cited as obstacles to pursuing cases. After sexual abuse, family disputes over custody were also common legal issues.

Kepler shipping data company reported that ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz dropped to six vessels on August 10. This number is a significant decrease compared to the recent daily average of 11 vessels. Before the war, about 130 to 140 ships used to pass through this strait daily.

Alireza Salimi stated that if countries in the Makkah defense pact attack Iran, the Islamic Republic will respond without hesitation. He said the pact has caused regional insecurity and that Saudi Arabia seeks allies through financial influence. Salimi also referred to Iran's strong responses to some Gulf countries.

The Stockholm International Peace Research Institute reported that South Korea has increased its arms exports. Seoul has expanded its market share with competitive prices and advanced technology. South Korea's defense cooperation with Middle Eastern countries, especially the UAE and Saudi Arabia, has increased.

A citizen sent a video showing the grave of Hamidreza Rouhi, a protester killed in the Woman, Life, Freedom uprising. He says the immortal ones will not forget the path of freedom. The video was sent to Iran International.

Images show that the football field at Azadi Stadium is undergoing turf substructure work. The previous turf was removed weeks ago. The sports facilities management decided to replace the turf with hybrid grass.

Due to a threat from the Islamic Republic to assassinate Donald Trump, a secret security operation was carried out in Turkey last month. Trump was secretly transferred by a catering truck to a military plane and flown to Britain. This operation took place on July 8, after Trump's trip to Ankara for the NATO summit.

The Makkah defense pact was signed between Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey. Pakistan's Prime Minister Shahbaz Sharif stated that the goal of this pact is to achieve peace among all Islamic countries. This news was discussed in an interview with Javad Hamdani, a journalist from Iran International.

Sanaz Mehrabi Dashtaki, a 15-year-old girl from Dashtak village in Marvdasht county, was killed by her uncle using a hunting rifle. This news was reported by the HRANA news agency. The identity of the victim has been confirmed by HRANA.

Ahmad Bakhshayesh Ardestani stated that the defense pact of Mecca between Pakistan, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia is more symbolic than operational. He said Saudi Arabia tries to buy security with money and, due to the US's inability to defend itself, has to ally with Pakistan and Turkey. Bakhshayesh Ardestani believes Pakistan and Turkey are unlikely to go to war with Iran on behalf of the US.

Nurses and medical staff at Hakim Hospital in Nishapur held a protest today. They demanded attention to issues such as unpaid wage arrears, lack of equipment and personnel, mandatory overtime, and discrimination in bonus payments. They also called for revisions to nursing tariffs.

Iran International audiences reported a significant increase in the prices of psychiatric drugs, especially rare ones. Some foreign drugs for treating depression and anxiety have become scarce. Babak Khatti, a pediatrician, cited market monopoly and lack of effective supervision as causes of drug shortages.
A citizen sent a video showing garbage accumulation in the alleys of Nasaji Town in Kermanshah. The video was sent to Iran International. The issue concerns the waste situation in this area.

Navid Zarebin Irani, a Bahá'í citizen detained during the December 2025 protests, has been held without a judicial decision in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad for over six months. His case is still under review at the General and Revolutionary Prosecutor's Office in Mashhad, and no court hearing date has been set. His family has expressed concern about his uncertain situation.

A group of mountaineers commemorated the immortal names of the national revolution by climbing Alam Kuh peak. A video of this climb has been released. This act was done to honor the national revolution.

Mojtaba Maleki was elected as the president of the Bodybuilding Federation. In the first round of voting, Maleki received 19 votes and Mohammad Nasiri 12 votes. In the second round, Maleki won with 35 out of 51 votes for a four-year term.

The deputy prosecutor of Ardabil announced that the prosecutor's office will soon take action against the sale of clothing deemed against religious law or public decency. Supervision over coffeehouses and cafes has been intensified, resulting in the closure of three cafes and the arrest of 16 people. These measures aim to address disrespect to values and violations of laws.

Yossi Cohen, former head of Mossad, stated that Mossad agents have repeatedly entered the Fordow nuclear site to inspect it. He described the US attack on Fordow as the fulfillment of his dreams. He also said that 60% enriched uranium is still far from being used to make a bomb.

The Iranian Football League Organization announced that Khodadad Azizi's suspension has been lifted by the Football Federation's Appeals Committee. He can be present on the bench for Tractor's first week match against Paykan. This pardon came after his name was listed among the suspended players the previous day.

The Court of Appeals of Isfahan Province confirmed the five-year prison sentence of Mahshad Keshani, a student and detainee of the December 2025 protests. Mahshad Keshani is imprisoned in Dolatabad Prison in Isfahan. This sentence has been confirmed as is.

US forces fired on a Panama-flagged ship attempting to pass through the blockade of Iranian ports. The incident occurred early Tuesday, and the ship caught fire after being hit by a missile, which was later extinguished. All 17 crew members have been accounted for.

Ali Ahmadi, a 71-year-old retired teacher, remains detained in Adelabad prison in Shiraz since his arrest on March 5, with concerns about his health. He faces charges including corruption on earth and cooperation with Mossad, and his case has not progressed significantly. His family is also facing financial difficulties due to his continued detention.

Burhan Can Terzi, a Turkish journalist, was arrested by order of the Bakirkoy prosecutor for publishing false news about Jamal Musiala joining Galatasaray. Despite the club's denial, he maintained his claim. Istanbul police arrested him yesterday.

Mohsen Rezaee stated that the Islamic Republic will not retreat in the face of threats. Decisions must be stronger than before and made with precise understanding of conditions. Foreign policy includes strengthening deterrence, countering enemy pressure, and utilizing diplomatic capacity.
A citizen posted a video reporting the sluggish state of the fruit and vegetable market in Karaj. A merchant said the market is ruined and all the goods remain unsold.

Shahriar Shams, a expelled student from Tehran North Azad University, was arrested by security forces on Monday, 19th of Mordad, at his family home. His personal belongings, including his phone and laptop, were confiscated. His place of detention is unknown.

Mohsen Dehnavi announced that members of the Expediency Discernment Council recently elected Mohammad Mokhber and Mohammad Forouzandeh as replacements for Ali Larijani and Abdolrahim Mousavi in the High Supervisory Board for the proper implementation of general policies. The meeting was held on Tuesday, 20th of Mordad.

Donald Trump stated that Washington has cleared mines in the Strait of Hormuz and has full control over the area. He also said that the United States has full control over the financial assets of the Islamic Republic. These statements were reported by Samira Gharaei.

Majid Ibn al-Reza and Dato Seri Mohammad Khalid Nordin discussed expanding defense and military cooperation between Iran and Malaysia in a phone call. Ibn al-Reza identified experience transfer and technological cooperation as suitable areas for developing relations. He also described Israel as the main source of instability in the region.

Mohsin Naqvi, Pakistan's Interior Minister, met with Abbas Araghchi, Iran's Foreign Minister, in Tehran on Tuesday, August 11. Eskandar Momeni, Iran's Interior Minister, welcomed his Pakistani counterpart. Pakistan has acted as a mediator in Tehran-Washington talks, and the Pakistani Interior Minister has visited Iran several times recently.
A citizen reported in a video to Iran International that the refrigerator at home is completely empty. He also mentioned having a small child at home. The video was sent on Tuesday, August 11.

Donald Trump outlined three US strategies for the Islamic Republic, including naval blockade, economic pressure, and hard strikes. He said economic pressure is currently being implemented and the Islamic Republic faces severe economic problems. Trump called the Islamic Republic's negotiators deceitful.

The Lebanese parliament abolished the death penalty and replaced it with life imprisonment. Only the Hezbollah faction opposed this decision. The Lebanese Minister of Justice described this move as a historic step.

Rising prices and reduced purchasing power have made going to cafes and restaurants an expensive leisure activity for many citizens. Audiences say this leisure has been removed or limited from the budgets of many families. This issue was discussed with Baharan Azadi from Iran International.

The Pakistani defense minister stated that Iran and the United States are close to some form of agreement. These remarks were made in an interview with Bloomberg. Additionally, the Pakistani interior minister has traveled to Tehran.

An American official and maritime security sources have reported that a Panama-flagged container ship was targeted in the Sea of Oman. The American official stated that the ship ignored warnings to stop and was attempting to break the naval blockade of Iranian ports. The Wall Street Journal also reported, citing an American official, that a US military helicopter fired at the ship's rudder.

A senior Canadian officer was awarded a military medal for coordinating the evacuation of 10,000 troops from the Qatar base during Iranian attacks. This has raised questions about Canada's involvement in Middle East conflicts and the transparency of its Ministry of Defense. Canadian officials had previously denied direct involvement of their forces in these battles.
